sections.title: An Australian heath shrub
sections.text: Woollsia pungens is an erect, prickly shrub of eastern Australia, usually 20–100 cm tall and occasionally reaching 2 m. Its small, sharply pointed leaves sit close to the stems. The image's narrow pointed foliage and pink, tubular, scented flowers match the species; the flowers are about 8–13 mm across.

sections.title: Flowers and habitat
sections.text: Flowers range from white to dark pink and are borne among the upper leaves; the small fruit is about 2.5 mm across. It grows in heath and dry sclerophyll forest, often on sandstone or coastal dunes. The cited flora gives no established food use, so no part is described as edible.
